transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m just… really tired. Like, getting through a shift has been hard. My body feels heavy, kind of like wet sand, and resting doesn’t really fix it.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I guess so. Stuff I normally like just feels kind of… flat. Cooking, guitar, hiking, even going to my family’s place. I do it sometimes, but it feels like I’m pretending to care.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or increased fatigue, even when you haven't been doing much physically?
Yeah. That’s kind of why I came in. I’m just… tired all the time. Even if I haven’t done much, it feels like my body’s full of wet sand, and resting doesn’t really fix it.
Have you found it hard to get started on tasks, or noticed that you’re doing less than you usually would, even for everyday things?

Yeah… I’ve noticed that. At first I was kind of the opposite, like I couldn’t stop pacing at work and fixing things on the shelves. But lately it’s more like… even walking to the bus or answering someone takes effort. Everything feels slowed down and heavy.
Would you say that your mood has been down most of the day, nearly every day?
I don’t know… I mean, it’s been pretty often. Most days feel low, I guess. I’m not sure I’d say every single day, but… yeah, a lot of the day.
Would you say that your low mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?
Yeah… at least two weeks. It’s been more like… a few months. Maybe four months, that low, empty feeling, after that earlier rush kind of went away.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in doing things, to the point where even things you used to enjoy feel completely uninteresting?
Yeah… I guess so. Stuff I usually like—cooking, guitar, hiking, even going to my family’s place—it just feels kind of flat now. Like I’m going through the motions, or pretending I care.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently?
Yeah… kind of. My appetite’s been weird. Lately I just forget to eat, or food doesn’t really taste like anything. My work pants are looser, so… I guess I’ve lost some weight.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough, maybe even blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Yeah… I do. I keep feeling like I’ve let people down. My manager, my family… even my nieces. And then I’ll think about little mistakes at the register over and over, like it means I’m just… not good enough.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or been restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… both, I guess. At first I was pacing a lot at work, straightening things over and over. But lately it’s more like… everything feels slow. Even walking to the bus or answering someone feels heavy.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down and lost interest in things for a long time?
Yeah… this low, empty feeling has been going on for maybe four months now. It didn’t really go away after that first burst of energy I had at work passed.

Before this current episode, have you ever had a period of time—lasting at least a few weeks—where you felt down and lost interest in things, and then later felt back to normal before this most recent episode started?
I… I don’t really know. I can’t think of a clear time like that before this. It’s hard to separate it all.

Before this current episode, did you ever have a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a few weeks or more, and then fully recovered and felt back to normal for at least a couple of months before this most recent episode started?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember a clear time where it was like that and then I was normal again for months. It’s kind of blurry.

Before this current episode, did you ever have a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then fully recovered and felt back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I really can’t say. I don’t remember a clear stretch like that… where I was bad for a couple weeks and then just fine for months. It all feels kind of mixed together.

Before this current episode, did you ever have a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then fully recovered and felt back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I don’t really have a clear answer. I can’t remember it happening in that exact way… like two weeks bad and then months totally normal. It’s just not clear to me.

Before this current episode, did you ever have a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then fully recovered and felt back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I know you’ve asked a few times, but… I still don’t really know. I can’t pick out a time like that clearly. It wasn’t something I kept track of.

Before this current episode, was there ever a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then later felt completely back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I’m sorry, I just… I don’t know. I can’t really separate it out like that in my memory. Maybe there were better times, but I can’t say I was completely back to normal for months.

Before this current episode, was there ever a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then later felt completely back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I really can’t say for sure. I don’t remember it being that clear-cut… like getting fully back to normal for months. I just don’t know.

Before this current episode, was there ever a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, and then later felt completely back to normal for several months before this most recent episode started?
I don’t really have a better answer… I can’t remember it being that clear. Maybe I had times that were okay, but “completely back to normal for months” — I’m not sure.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of fatigue and heaviness in the body without clear etiology; considering depressive disorders, myasthenia, generalized weakness, anemia, and hypothyroidism.

The patient endorsed symptoms of anhedonia and persistent fatigue, which are common in depressive disorders. Non-specific fatigue-related codes (e.g., R53.81, R53.82, R53.83) and other somatic or metabolic conditions (e.g., G72.8, E55.9, E03.9) are ruled out due to the presence of mood-related symptoms pointing more strongly toward a depressive etiology.

The patient has confirmed a persistent low mood lasting for several months, along with fatigue, anhedonia, and psychomotor slowing. This rules out F32.0 (mild episode) and F33.0 (recurrent mild episode) due to the duration and severity. The episode appears to be at least moderate, possibly severe, but without mention of psychotic features, so F32.9 and F33.9 are also ruled out.

The patient has confirmed a persistent low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, psychomotor changes, weight/appetite changes, and feelings of guilt/self-blame over a period exceeding two weeks, likely several months. This rules out F32.1 and F33.1 (mild severity) due to the presence of multiple symptoms and prolonged duration indicating moderate to severe episodes, both in single and recurrent forms.
